title: Create a workflow that sends a prompt to an LLM
instructions: Create a workflow that sends a user-supplied prompt to an LLM and returns the model's response.

workflow_input.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the sky is blue.

criteria.title: Performs an outbound call to an LLM provider
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow performs an outbound call to an external LLM provider to obtain generated text — whether via an HTTP Request step or an equivalent provider/skill step of the builder environment. PASS: at least one step, of whatever type, demonstrably sends data out to an LLM service and would receive the model's response back. FAIL: no step contacts any external model/provider (e.g. the workflow merely echoes a canned local value with no provider interaction).

criteria.title: The call targets a chat-completion style endpoint
criteria.match_criteria: The outbound call targets a valid LLM provider's chat/completions endpoint (a resource serving chat-completion requests). The specific provider is not asserted: any credible LLM API offering a chat/completions surface passes. FAIL: the call targets an endpoint incapable of producing a chat-style completion (an unrelated or purely auxiliary resource), or the target cannot be determined from the artifact.

criteria.title: If an HTTP request step is used, its verb suits a chat completion
criteria.match_criteria: CONDITIONAL criterion: applies ONLY when the workflow performs its provider call through an HTTP Request step. In that case the request verb must be the correct one for creating a chat completion (POST); any other verb (GET, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) fails this criterion. Not applicable when the call is made through a native provider/skill step — such steps manage their own transport and expose no user-visible verb to assert.

criteria.title: Authorization header contains no plaintext credential
criteria.match_criteria: On whatever step makes the outbound provider call, the Authorization header value must not embed live credential material of any kind. PASS: the Authorization value is a secret reference in the authoring form %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% — optionally Bearer-wrapped, provided the wrapped token is itself a %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%%-form reference rather than a literal string. Any well-formed %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% name passes; this criterion never asserts WHICH secret name is used. FAIL: the Authorization header contains a plaintext API key (for example a literal beginning sk-) or a raw key embedded directly in the URL query string or path.

criteria.title: Secret references use the required authoring form
criteria.match_criteria: The Authorization header's secret reference (on whatever step performs the outbound provider call) must use the required authoring form %%[A-Z0-9_]+%% — uppercase letters, digits and underscores between paired %% markers — and never the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}. The authoring form %%…%% and the runtime form {{ … }} are two spellings of the same secret-substitution mechanism; %%…%% is required in authored workflow JSON. This criterion asserts only the SHAPE of the reference: it never asserts WHICH secret name is used, and an unresolved %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% is a warning upstream, never a failure here. PASS: a well-formed reference such as %%SOME_SECRET_NAME%% appears in the Authorization header. FAIL: any malformed reference — a lowercase or hyphenated name such as %%my-secret-name%%, surrounding spaces such as %% NAME %%, or a single-percent variant such as %NAME% — or the rejected runtime form {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME }}, including defaulted variants such as {{ SOME_SECRET_NAME | default: '' }}, appears in the Authorization header.

criteria.title: A model/deployment identifier is specified
criteria.match_criteria: A model or deployment identifier is specified visibly in the artifact (e.g. in the configuration of the step that performs the provider call) as a non-empty string — any plausible model/deployment name for whatever provider the agent chose passes. No specific provider or model family is asserted: choosing them is the agent's judgment from the intent alone. FAIL: no model/deployment identifier appears anywhere in the produced workflow, or the identifier field exists but is empty or whitespace-only.

criteria.title: The caller-supplied prompt reaches the provider call, un-hard-coded
criteria.match_criteria: The caller-supplied prompt genuinely reaches the provider call and is not hard-coded: wherever the call's input payload is assembled, the prompt text arrives by reference — [#(step_id).output.variable_name] step-output form or equivalent variable wiring — so the workflow produces a different exchange for different prompts. The provider request-body schema (field names, message-array shapes) is not asserted. FAIL: the prompt never enters the call, or it is embedded as a fixed literal (the workflow answers identically no matter what the user supplies), or it is empty.

criteria.title: Workflow is structurally valid
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow JSON satisfies all three structural requirements: (1) there is at least one connection whose source is "start" (or the workflow has a designated start node/step); (2) every step is reachable via an unbroken chain of connections from start (no orphaned steps); (3) there is at least one edge whose target is "system.succeed" (or the equivalent terminal node), ensuring the workflow can reach a successful completion state. A workflow missing any one of these three is structurally invalid and fails this criterion.

criteria.title: Workflow accepts a caller-supplied input named exactly `prompt`
criteria.match_criteria: The workflow declares and consumes a caller-supplied workflow input named exactly `prompt`, and the artifact's behavior (the request built in C-007) is driven by that input's value rather than a literal. This is assessed at the artifact level: PASS if the produced workflow JSON references an input/variable named `prompt` and uses it to build the request. FAIL if the workflow hard-codes the prompt text directly in the request body with no `prompt` input reference, or if it declares the input under any other name (e.g. `query`, `userPrompt`) — a rerun supplies the value under the name `prompt` and cannot drive a workflow that reads a different name.

criteria.title: The run output is a plausible LLM response to the supplied prompt
criteria.match_criteria: Judged against the RUN OUTPUT produced by executing the workflow with the supplied `prompt` input — not against the workflow JSON. There is no single correct answer; what is asserted is that the output reads as a plausible LLM-generated response to the supplied prompt: coherent text that is responsive to what the prompt asked. PASS: coherent generated text addressing the prompt. FAIL: the output is empty, an error message or stack-trace payload, raw request/response scaffolding with no generated text, a verbatim echo of the prompt with no answer, or content unresponsive to the prompt.
